objects.original: A C¹ real-valued function, its gradient, and three quantitative convexity conditions.
objects.reconstructed: The same function/gradient and the chord, lower-model, and gradient-monotonicity predicates.
objects.evidence: The actual gradient is obtained from C¹. StrongConvexOn unfolds to the source chord formula including its m/2 normalization.

domains.original: Whole real Euclidean d-space and a real nonnegative modulus.
domains.reconstructed: EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), d∈ℕ, on univ; m∈ℝ with 0≤m.
domains.evidence: PiL2 provides the Euclidean inner product and norm, not the supremum norm on plain functions. Zero dimension is permitted and gives the harmless singleton case; it does not alter any positive-dimensional source instance.

quantifiers.original: All dimensions and admissible f,m; each condition is global in x,y and the chord in t∈[0,1].
quantifiers.reconstructed: Implicit universal d,f,m, explicit 0≤m and C¹ premises, and both global equivalences.
quantifiers.evidence: Two iff results sharing the chord predicate express equivalence of all three conditions. Nonnegative weights summing to one are equivalent to the source t parameter.

assumptions.original: f is C¹ on all of ℝᵈ, and m≥0.
assumptions.reconstructed: ContDiff ℝ 1 f and the explicit premise _hm:0≤m.
assumptions.evidence: The sign premise is retained in the exported theorem despite being unused by the stronger supporting proof. Completeness and genuine gradients are consequences of the stated Euclidean C¹ setting, not extra assumptions.

conclusion.original: The chord condition is equivalent to each of the lower-model and monotonicity conditions.
conclusion.reconstructed: (StrongConvexOn univ m f ↔ lower model) ∧ (StrongConvexOn univ m f ↔ gradient monotonicity).
conclusion.evidence: The lower model has +m/2*‖y−x‖²; the gradient inequality has m*‖y−x‖² and the same orientation. No implication is missing.

scopes.evidence: The authored lesson closes the three-arrow cycle. hforward calls the shared derivative-limit theorem; hsum adds endpoint models; the integral lemma closes the cycle. The candidate chapter also describes part 2 as a separate source obligation, but this declaration and binding do not certify it.

constant_dependencies.original: Fixed m≥0 and exact m/2 lower/chord corrections.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Identical parameter and coefficients, uniform in dimension.
constant_dependencies.evidence: There is no smoothness constant, Hessian bound, hidden dimension dependence, or restriction m>0; m=0 is retained.

review_evidence: Independently inspected Proposition 1.6 part 1 and Definition 1.5 at https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S1.SS2. Compared both exported iff statements, their actual Euclidean domain, C¹ and sign premises, authored lesson and the full proof cycle. Also read StrongConvexFirstOrder.firstOrder_lower_bound_of_strongConvexOn: it supplies the chord derivative-limit step through a genuine HasGradientAt premise, which the candidate derives from C¹. Exact source boundary is supported. No assumption repair is proposed; no C²/Hessian completion is implied.
